messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 metering anomaly detected in prod — token counts non-monotonic on emitter -> usage pipeline. Paging @oncall. Dashboard: https://redwood.app/incidents/1719982468 :rotating_light:
Lee: Ack, I'm on it. Jumping into the billing pipeline now. @Maria can you confirm customer impact (overage emails / delayed reports)?
Maria: Seeing a cluster of overage flags for 3 customers in eu-west. UI shows delayed usage for ~2h. Unsure if duplicates or rewinded offsets.
Devraj: Looking at kafka: partition-3 shows offsets moving backward intermittently after high-backpressure window. Quick tail:
```
$ kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group usage-consumer
TOPIC   PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET 
usage   3          1245873
```
But producer logs show retries with same event_id around restart.
Kai: Support: 2 customers opened tickets about sudden charges. Recommend pausing overage emails until we confirm.
Lee: Pausing alerts now: `POST /internal/alerts/pause?scope=billing_incidents` -> done. Confirmed via alerts service: paused. :white_check_mark:
Maria: Exporting affected window for recon: `SELECT event_id, customer_id, tokens, ts FROM usage_events WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-03-20T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-20T04:00:00Z' AND topic = 'usage'`
Results show ~14k events with matching event_id duplicates across same customer and identical payload.
Devraj: Likely producer retry bug when emitter restarted under backpressure. Preparing hotfix `emitter:fix/retry-idempotency-2026-03-20`. Will canary at 10% traffic.
incident-bot: Deploy job started for emitter hotfix. Canary 10% -> 25% -> 100%. CI link: https://ci.redwood.app/12345 :gear:
Lee: Good. After canary stable, plan to hold billing window close and run dedupe backfill before resuming alerts. Maria, can you draft customer comms?
Maria: Drafting now: "We're investigating an issue that caused duplicate usage records which may have triggered overage emails. We've paused billing alerts and are reconciling charges. We'll correct any incorrect charges and follow up with details"
Kai: Support will hold off outbound customer replies until you say go. We can offer refunds for affected accounts.
Devraj: Canary 10% looks clean for 15m, no backward offsets observed on partition-3. Increasing to 25%.
Lee: Once 25% stable for 5m we'll kick the dedupe dry-run:
```
$ python tools/dedupe_backfill.py --dry-run --start 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z --end 2026-03-20T04:00:00Z --key event_id
```
Maria: Dry-run shows ~13.8k duplicate token events to remove across 3 customers. Expected token delta per-customer: small but enough to trigger alerts.
Kai: I'll prep templated messages and put affected customers on a priority list. Waiting on final counts before sending.
incident-bot: Canary progressed to 100% and completed successfully.
Devraj: Hotfix deployed to 100%. Monitoring consumer lag and offsets. No regressions so far.
Lee: Starting dedupe backfill (non-destructive mode first). ETA ~18m. I'll remain oncall and keep thread updated.
Maria: Backfill finished. Dedupe removed 13,842 duplicate token events. Recomputed billing shows corrected usage below overage thresholds for affected accounts.
Kai: Support: notifying customers now with apology + refund plan. Templates used: refunded hours.
Devraj: Root cause: emitter retry logic could re-emit identical events when restart coincided with broker backpressure. Follow-up ticket INF-712 created and assigned to me for making emitter idempotent at the producer level.
Maria: Recommend a short postmortem: include offset traces, affected customers, why alerts fired, and a mitigation plan (idempotency + stronger alert gating).
Lee: Oncall clear. Closing pager for this incident. Great work all. :tada:
